I faced similar problem while using Grep and Glob tool.
I solved in this way:

```
Both Grep and Glob tools depend on Ripgrep. When ripgrep is not installed, the tool automatically downloads it from GitHub:
// ripgrep.ts line 147-150
const response = await fetch(url)  // url = https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/...
Root cause: Network failure when downloading ripgrep from GitHub.
Solution:
1. Install ripgrep manually: brew install ripgrep (macOS) or apt install ripgrep (Linux)
2. Or ensure your network can access github.com
Run rg --version to check if ripgrep is installed.
```

We have a complementary PR at #16695 that tackles the in-memory side of these leaks — event listener accumulation in the TUI, unbounded Maps/Sets in the bus/RPC/LSP subsystems, timer/interval cleanup, and session data not being freed on switch. Between the two PRs, most of the memory growth paths should be covered.

This overlaps with our PR #16695 on the LSP diagnostics and session/prompt fixes, but you are catching stuff we missed — the plugin Bus.subscribeAll() stacking and the msgs array retention in prompt processing. Also see #16730 which tackles the database/storage side. Between the three PRs this should cover most of the memory growth paths.

Thanks for flagging! Checked #16695 — there are 3 overlapping files but the changes are complementary:

- **`lsp/client.ts`**: Both PRs delete empty diagnostics entries. #16695 goes further with a 200-file LRU cap and `clear()` on shutdown — that's a superset of our change here, so no conflict. Happy to defer to theirs on this file.
- **`util/rpc.ts`**: Different code paths — ours adds a 60s timeout on `pending` calls (prevents leaked promises from dead workers), theirs cleans up empty `listeners` Sets (prevents tombstones). Both are needed and merge cleanly.
- **`session/prompt.ts`**: Different areas — ours is the output spooling rewrite (~line 1637), theirs rejects pending callbacks on cancel (~line 262). No overlap.

The rest is non-overlapping: our PR covers database health (auto-vacuum, WAL checkpoint, incremental vacuum), bash output spooling, compaction data clearing, Levenshtein optimization, FileTime cleanup, and session retention. Their PR covers TUI event listener leaks, bus tombstones, PTY buffer cleanup, model refresh interval, and share-next disposal.

Between the two PRs most memory growth paths should indeed be covered 👍

I went through every open memory leak PR on this repo. What I found is, frankly, unacceptable.

23 open PRs. 20+ contributors. 0 merged. 63 days and counting.

The community has been screaming about this since January. Here's what's been sitting unreviewed:

@hendem submitted Bus subscription disposal fixes on January 6th. Had to rebase and resubmit on Jan 12th because the PR rotted. Got 30 review comments but still never merged. 63 days and counting.

@sauerdaniel opened 6 PRs in a single day on January 17th. SDK event listener cleanup (#8254), OAuth transport leaks (#9145), ACP session cleanup (#9146), TUI event listener leaks (#9147), timeout/interval cleanup (#9148), and Instance disposal chain (#9149). Every single one: 0 reviews, 0 comments. 52 days of complete silence.

@ztripez submitted a 15-file mega-fix on January 24th covering LRU caches, prompt loop cloning, pending timeouts, and more (#10392). 0 reviews, 0 comments. 45 days.

@Stranmor added TTL and LRU eviction across ACP sessions, Instance cache, LSP clients, and PTY ring buffers on February 5th (#12259). 0 reviews, 0 comments. 32 days.

@dzianisv reported 100GB+ RAM leading to a macOS crash from O(n²) string concatenation in processor.ts on February 11th (#13186). 0 reviews, 0 comments. 26 days.

@sebishogun, @feelsodev, @kryptobaseddev, @lytedev, @tda1017, @brendandebeasi, @NachoFLizaur, @dimaosipa, @GooseG17, @sjawhar, @jmylchreest, @BYK all submitted fixes between February and March. Almost all of them: 0 reviews, 0 comments.

15 out of 23 PRs have literally zero engagement from maintainers. No reviews. No comments. No "thanks, we'll look at this." No "this conflicts with internal work." Nothing.

Because nothing gets merged, contributors keep independently discovering and fixing the same bugs. lsp/client.ts has been independently fixed 7 times across 7 different PRs (#13594, #14650, #15435, #15646, #16346, #16695, #16730). session/prompt.ts, also 7 times. bus/index.ts, 6 times. tool/bash.ts, 5 times. plugin/index.ts, 5 times. app.tsx, 4 times. That's 20+ people writing the same fixes for the same bugs because the first person's fix was never reviewed.

Meanwhile, users are reporting:
- 16.4 GB RSS in a 3-hour session (#7049, reported Jan 6, 63 days ago)
- 100GB+ RAM causing macOS crashes (#13186, reported Feb 11)
- 15GB over 24 hours leading to a kernel panic (#16241, reported Mar 5)
- 2.3 GB/min virtual memory growth (#16346)
- 2.9GB+ per session in serve mode (#16616)
- 1.99 GB SQLite database with no cleanup whatsoever (#16730)

People are having their operating systems crash. Their laptops are thermal throttling. They're restarting opencode every couple hours as a workaround for bugs that were fixed by the community months ago.

The fixes exist. All 23 of them. They just need to be merged.

A maintainer needs to triage these PRs, identify the best version of each fix (since many overlap), coordinate the rebasing, and start shipping. The longer this waits, the worse the merge conflicts get, and the more contributors give up and walk away.

Related PRs for reference: #7032, #7049, #7914, #8254, #9145, #9146, #9147, #9148, #9149, #10392, #12259, #13186, #13194, #13514, #13594, #14650, #15326, #15435, #15646, #15757, #16241, #16346, #16616, #16628, #16695, #16730

> Got this working on Ghostty + tmux (Linux). Two things were needed:
> 
> **1. OpenCode keybinds config (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json):**
> 
> ```
> {
>   keybinds: {
>     input_submit: return,
>     input_newline: shift+return
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> **2. tmux extended keys (~/.tmux.conf):**
> 
> ```
> set -g extended-keys on
> set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'
> ```
> 
> Then reload tmux config: `tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf`
> 
> The root cause in a tmux setup is that even if the terminal (Ghostty) sends Shift+Enter correctly via the kitty keyboard protocol, tmux strips the extended key sequence before it reaches OpenCode. The extended-keys on setting tells tmux to pass those sequences through. Without it, shift+enter behaves like plain enter, which is why it was submitting instead of inserting a newline.

This worked for me, thanks.

Pasting didn't work at all for me in OpenCode (using the kitty terminal emulator).

I dug into the code and noticed that **OpenCode only handles image pasting** internally. See the [`input_paste`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/1db292f4df3bd69d4262ca6471aa5879b83b1fd1/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx#L203) action. It silently ignores any pasted text.

It's a bit confusing that the action is called `input_paste` even though it doesn't paste text. Something like `input_image_paste` might be clearer…

As far as I can tell, text pasting is left entirely to the terminal emulator.

So I configured `kitty.conf` like this (you need to adapt this to the terminal emulator you're using):

```
# paste from system clipboard (and still send the key)
map ctrl+y combine : send_key ctrl+y : paste_from_clipboard
```

With this setup, kitty pastes the clipboard text while OpenCode still receives the key event, so image pasting continues to work. Note that I have this in my `tui.jsonc`:

```jsonc
  "keybinds": {
    "input_paste": "ctrl+y",
  },
```

It might be worth updating the [Copy/paste not working on Linux](https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/#copypaste-not-working-on-linux) and/or [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/docs/keybinds/) sections. There are quite a few copy/paste related issues in the tracker, so clarifying this could save others from having to read the code to understand what's going on.

A workaround for this is to edit your `/etc/hosts` file and add a line like
```
127.0.0.1 remote-server
```

Then you can connect to your remote server as `remote-server:4096` even though it's just an alias for localhost. Opencode will think you're accessing a remote and give you the web-based filepicker as expected. Not a great workaround, but it does work.
